public_art.title: Boy III
public_art.medium: cast bronze with white patina finish
public_art.access: Artwork is accessible during normal business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m.; artwork is visible from Howard Street
public_art.detail: Thomas Houseago, born in Leeds, England in 1972, cast Boy III and its companion Sleeping Boy in white-coated bronze, a departure from the plaster he traditionally worked in.

public_art.title: Sleeping Boy
public_art.access: artwork is accessible during normal business hours, 8:00 a.m to 7:00 p.m; artwork is visible from Howard Street
public_art.detail: Sleeping Boy is the reclining companion piece to Boy III; both are cast in white-coated bronze with casting marks left intentionally unsmoothed by the artist.

historical_record.description: A one-storey concrete industrial building of 1921 stood on this parcel until it was cleared for the third building of Foundry Square. The present building dates from 2014.
The building then on this site came down late in the year, and a permit was granted for two years of interim parking on the cleared lot. The present building dates from 2014.
The Board of Permit Appeals upheld the Department of Public Works and allowed the permit to demolish the building at 515 Howard Street to stand. The present building dates from 2014.
An existing surface parking lot then occupied part of a vacant site.

historical_record.headline: KPMG Shrinks Office by a Third to Join Anthropic on San Francisco's New 'AI Alley'
